questions.q:
With reference to the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), which replaced the earlier rural employment programme from 1 July 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Costs are shared between the Centre and the north-eastern and Himalayan States in the ratio 90:10.
2. Works are chosen in open Gram Sabha meetings without any prior plan, as under the earlier scheme.
3. The allowance payable if work is not given within 15 days of demand has been retained.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Other States share costs 60:40, whereas the Centre earlier paid all unskilled wages. Statement 2 is wrong: the new scheme is pre-planned, with works drawn from Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans linked to the PM GatiShakti master plan, which is why critics fear a loss of Gram Sabha autonomy. The guarantee has risen from 100 to 125 days.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Critics argue that the 2026 rural employment scheme weakens the right to work.
Statement-II: The new scheme is a pre-planned framework tied to village development plans, and work cannot begin if a State delays its share of funds.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. The earlier law was demand-driven: work had to be given when sought. The new design allocates work through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans linked to the PM GatiShakti master plan, and depends on State budgets. Civil society groups say this turns a right into an allocation and reduces the Gram Sabha's role in choosing works.

questions.q: Under the rural employment scheme that replaced the earlier guarantee programme in 2026, States may notify a pause in work of up to 60 days in a year. The purpose of this pause is to
o: allow audit of works before new ones are sanctioned
let States meet their share of funds before the next financial year
complete the shift of workers to the new digital payment system
avoid shortage of labour for farms during peak sowing and harvest
questions.e: Year-round availability of scheme work was said to draw labour away from farms at critical times, so the new scheme allows an aggregate pause of up to 60 days in peak seasons. Critics say this weakens it as an absolute fallback and reduces casual labourers' bargaining power over farm wages. A suggestion is to let block committees set the window to local crop calendars and suspend it during drought.

questions.q:
Which of the following are among the four priority verticals for asset creation under the rural employment scheme launched in 2026?
1. Water security
2. Core rural infrastructure
3. Livelihood infrastructure such as storage and cold chains
4. Urban housing for migrant workers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The four verticals are water security, core rural infrastructure such as all-weather roads, livelihood infrastructure such as storage, silos and cold chains, and climate-resilient infrastructure. Urban housing is outside a rural scheme. The aim is larger, durable assets in place of the small works of the earlier scheme, with a digital stack using biometrics and geospatial monitoring to curb fake muster rolls.

questions.q:
With reference to the transition to the new rural employment scheme in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. No funds were released to States until all of them had notified the new guidelines.
2. Every State has refused to notify the new guidelines because of the change in the funding pattern.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. An interim release of about Rs 95,700 crore was made to keep funds flowing, and over a hundred officials were sent to districts to prevent payment delays. More than twenty States notified the guidelines, and States ultimately made matching budget provisions despite the debate over cooperative federalism.

questions.q:
With reference to the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2016 and is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
2. It is implemented in all States and Union Territories without exception.
3. It works through self-help groups and their federations at village and cluster level.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. The Mission was launched in 2011, as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, under the Ministry of Rural Development. It does not operate in Delhi and Chandigarh, so statement 2 is wrong. It reaches about 10 crore households through about 91 lakh self-help groups organised into village and cluster federations.

questions.q: The 2026 evaluation of the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission, which found that only about 15 per cent of self-help groups had started group businesses, was commissioned by the
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office of NITI Aayog
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.e: The Office engaged a private research firm, which surveyed about 2,200 households in eleven States and two Union Territories as part of a package evaluating rural development schemes. Groups were often formed in haste to meet targets, loans went to housing, toilets and medical needs, and revolving funds were often shared out for consumption. Members avoided loans because they had no assured market for their products.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Fund under the rural livelihoods mission : Use
1. Revolving Fund : Strengthens the corpus of a self-help group for internal lending
2. Community Investment Fund : Support for income-generating and livelihood activities
3. Community Enterprise Fund : Consumption loans to individual members
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. A revolving fund is repaid and lent again; about three-quarters of respondents had access to it. Half received the community investment fund, up to Rs 2.5 lakh. Pair 3 is wrong: the enterprise fund is meant for larger ventures, and only about 4 per cent received it, which shows how little the Mission has moved from inclusion to enterprise.

questions.q:
With reference to the rural livelihoods mission, consider the following statements:
1. 'Participatory Identification of the Poor' is a community-led process for identifying vulnerable households.
2. 'Namo Drone Didi' trains and equips women's self-help groups to provide drone services to farmers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Participatory identification is considered more authentic than top-down surveys, but the evaluation found that groups were sometimes formed after it without any viable local business. Drone services, training for women farmers under Mahila Kisan programmes, and gender resource centres dealing with child marriage and domestic violence are among the ways the Mission empowers women.
